question: Does Ramapo offer any master's degrees? I already have a bachelor's from 2009 and I'm looking at going back.
answer:
Yes. The catalog lists these graduate degrees: Accounting MS, Applied Mathematics MS, Business Administration MBA, Computer Science MS, Creative Music Technology MFA, Data Science MS, Nursing MSN, Public Policy MPP, Social Work MSW, and Special Education MA. It also lists Nursing Practice DNP, which is a doctorate, not a master’s. [5] Graduate Admissions’ “Available Graduate Programs” page lists MBA, MS in Accounting, MS in Data Science, MSN, MA in Special Education, MSW, MS in Applied Mathematics, MS in Computer Science, and Master of Public Policy. The pages’ lists differ. [6]

The general requirements call for a baccalaureate degree from an accredited institution; they do not specify how recently it must have been earned. A 3.0 GPA or above is recommended. [8] The catalog says applicants usually present a minimum 3.0 GPA, and all programs require an official transcript verifying the completed accredited bachelor’s degree and at least one recommendation letter. [17]

To apply, submit the online Graduate Admissions Application and review general and program-specific requirements. [9] The general-requirements page says to pay a non-refundable $65 fee; an unpaid application is incomplete and will not be reviewed. [8] The application page allows a fee waiver, and the catalog says an application fee or approved waiver is required for review; the pages differ on the fee-waiver wording. [9][17] Apply online: https://apply.ramapo.edu/apply/ [15]. Official transcripts are sent electronically to graduate@ramapo.edu or mailed to Ramapo College of New Jersey, Attn: Admissions, 505 Ramapo Valley Road, Mahwah, NJ 07430. RCNJ alumni need not submit RCNJ transcripts. [8]

Contact Graduate Admissions: graduate@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7270, McBride House. [7]

question: how many credits is the MBA program and are there any prerequisite courses if my undergrad wasnt in business
answer:
The Business Administration MBA is a Master of Business Administration. Its listed requirements include Foundational Courses: all six—ACCT 510 FOUNDATIONS OF ACCOUNTING, BADM 510 FOUNDATION STATS FOR BUSINESS, ECON 510 FOUNDATIONS OF ECONOMICS, FINC 510 FOUNDATIONS OF FINANCE, MGMT 510 FOUNDATIONS OF MANAGEMENT, and MKTG 510 FOUNDATIONS OF MARKETING. The 30-credit Advanced Standing Program does not require these foundational courses. [1]
For Advanced Standing, a bachelor’s degree in Business is required to qualify for the 30-credit program; a Business minor and/or completion of all foundation Business coursework may be considered with MBA Program Director approval. [4] The catalog requirement list does not state the total credits for the standard MBA. [1] Graduate Admissions handles MBA applications: graduate@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7270. [4]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SB-MBA-MBAD) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/graduate/requirements/)

question: Is there an accelerated bachelor's to master's option? Which programs have it and how many grad credits can you take as an undergrad?
answer:
Yes. The catalog describes two 4+1 options: Computer Science 4+1 (BS to MS in Computer Science) and Applied Mathematics 4+1 (BS to MS in Applied Mathematics). Both are designed for undergraduates in Computer Science BS, Data Science BS, or Mathematics BS; students in other disciplines may contact the Graduate Program Director about a 5-year plan. [1][2]

A 4+1 student may take up to three graduate courses, not to exceed 12 credits, while pursuing the undergraduate degree. [1][2] The policy adds that a 4+1 student needs permission from the graduate program Director for one additional course, may take up to 8 graduate credits per semester, and may not have more than 50% of their credit load in graduate courses. [8] Undergraduates not enrolled in a graduate program may take up to 8 graduate credits; to take more they must enroll in a 4+1 program. [6]

Older pages also list Accounting MS, Elementary/Special Education MA, Flex MBA, Social Work MSW, and Public Policy MPP as 4+1 programs, but those pages are for 2021–2022 and are past-term listings. [4][5]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BS-PMCS) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BS-PAPM) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/learn/academics/) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/admitted-students/academics/) [6](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#credit-load) [8](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#undergraduate-students-taking-graduate-courses)

question: I have a BA in English from another school. If I come back for a second bachelor's in nursing, do I still have to do all the gen ed requirements?
answer:
No. For students pursuing a second bachelor’s degree, “General Education Requirements and General Education Distribution areas are waived” and “Pathways is waived” [4]. You must complete the School Core requirements in the Catalog at enrollment, follow the Transferring of Academic Credit Policy, complete at least 50% of the new major’s credits at Ramapo, and meet the undergraduate residency requirement [4].

The accelerated BSN is for prospective students who hold a non-Nursing bachelor’s degree [1]. Its listed requirements include all Nursing Prerequisite (Bridge) courses and all Nursing Requirements; students need C+ or better in all Bridge courses to proceed to Nursing courses and C+ or better in all Nursing courses [1]. The waiver applies to general education; it does not waive those listed nursing program requirements [1, 4].

To pursue the second bachelor’s, apply through the Office of Admissions for the degree [4]. Admissions: admissions@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7300; McBride House [4].

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BSN-NURA) [4](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#second-bachelor-s-degree-requirements1)

question: Whats the maximum number of transfer credits I can bring into a graduate program at Ramapo?
answer:
There isn’t one fixed credit count for every graduate program: at most 25% of the credits required for your degree may be considered for transfer, including Graduate Prior Learning Assessment (GPLA) credits. Transfer courses must be from another accredited institution of higher education. [5][8][9]

A course taken elsewhere may be considered if its syllabus shows it is equivalent to a course in a Ramapo graduate program. You may submit an application for transfer credit, but acceptance criteria vary by program and the graduate program Director must approve the credits. [5][8][9]

Contact Graduate Admissions at graduate@ramapo.edu or (201) 684-7270, or consult your graduate program Director. [8][9]

Sources: [5](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#transferring-academic-credit1) [8](https://www.ramapo.edu/graduate/faqs/) [9](https://www.ramapo.edu/graduate/faqs/)

question: Is there an MS in Computer Science? what are the core courses and do I need calc to get in
answer:
Yes. Ramapo offers the Computer Science MS, a Master of Science, in the School of Science, Nursing, and Health [1].

Core courses (required): CMPS 531 DATA STRUCTURES & ALGORITHMS; CMPS 547 FOUNDATIONS OF COMPUTER SCIENCE; DATA 620 ETHICS IN DATA & COMPUTING [1].

The MSCS admissions page does not state that calculus is required for admission. It says applicants should have a bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Software Engineering, or a closely related field; a GPA of 3.0 or above is recommended. Applicants with unrelated degrees may be considered with significant relevant professional experience. Submit a 400-word personal statement and resume. One professional or academic recommendation letter is required, except it is waived for current Ramapo students graduating in 2027 and recent Ramapo graduates from 2025 and 2026. Enter the reference’s name and contact information in the online application’s “Recommendations” section; Ramapo sends the request, and the reference uploads the letter to the application portal. An interview with the Program Director may be required [2]. I don’t have verified information establishing whether calculus is required for admission; contact Graduate Admissions at graduate@ramapo.edu or (201) 684-7270 [2].

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-MS-CMPM) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/graduate/requirements/)

question: how many credits do i need at ramapo to finish a bachelors if im transferring in 64 credits from a community college 15 yrs ago
answer:
Ramapo requires at least 128 credits overall; accepted transfer credits count toward that total. Students entering from a two-year college must complete at least 63 credits at Ramapo, and some programs require more coursework [5,9,11]. The Registrar FAQ instead says at least 32 credits at Ramapo, while the Registrar graduation page says at least 48; the Catalog says at least 32 [9,10,12,13]. The pages differ on the Ramapo-credit minimum. Pages also differ on the two-year transfer cap: 64 credits [6] versus up to 65 [11]. If you earned an AA or AS at a New Jersey community college, 64 credits are eligible to transfer; Ramapo may award additional credit depending on your degree and eligible credits [3]. The catalog lists TRGD 199 AA/AS DEGREE COMPLETED EQUIVALENT as 4 credits, with no published prerequisites [3].

For transfer evaluation, only credits from an accredited college/university with a grade of C (2.0) or better are considered, and credit must be consistent with Ramapo’s curriculum; applicability to requirements is subject to transfer evaluation and advisement [11]. I don’t have verified information on whether your 15-year-old credits will be accepted. Contact the Office of Admissions at admissions@ramapo.edu or (201) 684-7300 about evaluation [11]. Review the number of credits with your adviser [13].

Sources: [3](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/TRGD199) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/adult-students/faqs/) [11](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#transferring-academic-credit1) [13](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/faq/)

question: Does the accounting minor have any 300 level courses? I want to know if i can do it as a post-bacc to sit for the CPA
answer:
Yes. The Accounting Minor includes ACCT 321 INTERMEDIATE ACCOUNTING I and ACCT 322 INTERMEDIATE ACCOUNTING II; its electives include ACCT 329 FEDERAL TAXATION I and ACCT 332 FEDERAL TAXATION II. It also lists 400-level electives. [1]

The catalog describes the minor as an option for Ramapo College students and says a minor is added to an undergraduate degree. [1][3] Post-baccalaureate students can attend as non-degree students and must include a diploma copy with their non-degree application. [5][6] The pages provided do not verify whether a post-bacc non-degree student can pursue this minor, or whether it would meet CPA eligibility requirements. The Accounting Club says advisors encourage students to accumulate 150 undergraduate credits toward a CPA license; it does not state the licensing requirements. [8]

For the minor/post-bacc question, contact the Anisfield School of Business: asb@ramapo.edu; (201) 684-7379, (201) 684-7380, or (201) 684-7378. For non-degree application guidance, contact Admissions at admissions@ramapo.edu or (201) 684-7300. [5][6]
